evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name: Matt Munoz; Moving day: Tuesday the sixth (next week); Route: 12701 Lowden Lane to 1050 East Eleventh Street, Suite 350; Approximate size: 25 boxes total, 11 desks in parts
evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo_absent: Rep never frames the call with a time-boxed ask or promise of a dependable quote. Instead jumps directly into probing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda_absent: Rep never asks 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' or equivalent. Goes straight to logistics.
evidence_quotes.final_concern_raised: Matt: 'It's literally just, yeah, just need manpower to take boxes from point A to point B, because I don't think gamble, I don't think Amazon could deliver all those up to the third floor.'
evidence_quotes.rep_acknowledge: Rep: 'Yup. Okay, sounds good. Yeah, nor would they, right.'—acknowledges but does not dig deeper or reflect back.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_routed: Rep: 'Alright, if you don't mind, I am going to reach out to my supervisor, because this is, I'm usually trained up to about 1700 square foot houses. I do offices once in a while so I just want them to definitely check my estimate, cause I don't want to overestimate or under estimate for you. Do you mind if I give you a call just back?' Rep escalates to supervisor before providing pricing, routing to a callback/followup rather than completing quote on this call.

top_strength: Brianne gathered all four core discovery basics cleanly (name, moving day, both addresses, box count and size profile) and correctly recognized the commercial move was outside her typical scope, escalating to supervisor rather than overextending.
coaching_note: On every call—even short intake or office pickups—lead with the quid pro quo framing and ask their agenda *before* diving into logistics, so you own the conversation and surface concerns early; you skipped both here and went straight to probing, missing a chance to uncover priorities that could have shaped the estimate.
